props.note: Bismarck's hull, repositioned 2026-09 to the H.M.S. Hood Association's 2001 expedition fix (48.15N, 16.117W; see sources.md for the position discrepancy this replaced and the residual depth-vs-terrain gap at this point). Length 251 m and beam 36 m are the ship's published overall dimensions (Wikipedia, data/landmarks.json wreck_meta). Height 15 m is an unsourced estimate for a battleship hull of this displacement; no source found publishes a keel-to-deck figure for the wreck. ends [prow, rounded]: surveys (kbismarck.com) describe the hull as largely intact and in surprisingly good condition, so this uses a pointed bow and a rounded stern rather than a torn 'cut' end; note that data/landmarks.json's own wreck_meta separately describes the bow as 'separated from main hull', which conflicts with the intact-hull account -- see sources.md. heading_deg 20 is arbitrary: no source found publishes the ship's actual compass orientation on the seabed.

Stands in for Bismarck's four detached main-battery (38 cm) gun turrets, which broke free during the sinking and came to rest roughly in a line down the seamount flank (kbismarck.org forum, citing 1989 and later survey accounts; Magellan's 2019 digital-twin survey). The engine's procedural kinds have no turret shape, so a debris cluster marks the general area; it does not depict the turrets' real form. No public coordinates were found for the individual turrets, so this placement, roughly 1.2 km up-slope (north-east, toward the seamount summit) of the hull, is illustrative only -- hence low confidence on the matching POI. Repositioned 2026-09 with the hull; see sources.md.
